1. This Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 08.09.2015 passed by the Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.338/2013, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, issue of negligence and liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to the death of Rohit Singhal in the motor accident, compensation to the tune of 6,05,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization has been awarded.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submitted that the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4790 2 MA-1123-2015 award is contrary to the settled principles of law and the evidence available on record, resulting in grant of grossly inadequate compensation.

It is contended that the learned Tribunal committed a serious error in assessing the future income of the deceased at an unreasonably low figure, ignoring the unrebutted evidence that the deceased was a second-year MCA student at ITM University, Gwalior, and was a well-educated person having Suresh Chandra Singhal vs Anil Kumar Jain on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141743042/
1 bright future prospects.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that deduction towards personal expenses has been wrongly made at 1/2 instead of 1/3, and the compensation awarded under the conventional heads as well as the rate of interest granted are inadequate.

Reliance has been placed upon the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Basanti Devi and Another vs. Divisional Manager, New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and Others , reported in 2022 ACJ 823, and Bhuvnesh Sharma and Others vs.
SBI General Insurance Co. Ltd. and Another , reported in 2026 (1) TAC 54 (SC).

sentences.text: Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of the evidence available on record and no interference is warranted.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.

So far as the judgments relied upon by learned counsel for the appellants are concerned, in Basanti Devi (supra), the deceased was a Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Technology, and in Bhuvnesh Sharma (supra), the deceased was a second year engineering student.

In the present case,
the deceased was a student of MCA (Second Semester) in ITM University.

Thus, though the income cannot be assessed on the basis of that of an unskilled labourer, considering his educational NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4790 3 MA-1123-2015 qualification and future prospects, this Court finds it just and reasonable to assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month.

8. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 40% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 has been rightly applied by the Claims Tribunal.

Also, in view of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs.
Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131 , the claimants are entitled to get compensation towards loss of consortium and loss of estate.
